Step by step, for a fully amortized loan

$$\text{PMT}=P\frac{r(1+r)^n}{(1+r)^n-1},\qquad 
r=\frac{\text{APR}}{12}$$

$$\text{Total interest}=n\cdot\text{PMT}-P$$
$$\text{Total cost}= \text{Total interest}+\text{origination fee}$$

$P=\$80{,}000$ for all loans.

**Loan A:** $6.9\%$ APR, $6$ years  
$r=0.069/12=0.00575$, $n=72$  
$\text{PMT}\approx \$1{,}360.08$  
Total payments $\approx \$97{,}925.93$  
Interest $\approx \$17{,}925.93$  
Fee $=1\%\times 80{,}000=\$800$  
Total cost $\approx \$18{,}725.93$

**Loan B:** $5.9\%$ APR, $4$ years  
$r=0.059/12\approx0.0049167$, $n=48$  
$\text{PMT}\approx \$1{,}875.14$  
Total payments $\approx \$90{,}006.56$  
Interest $\approx \$10{,}006.56$  
Fee $=3\%\times 80{,}000=\$2{,}400$  
Total cost $\approx \$12{,}406.56$

**Loan C:** $7.9\%$ APR, $3$ years  
$r=0.079/12\approx0.0065833$, $n=36$  
$\text{PMT}\approx \$2{,}503.22$  
Total payments $\approx \$90{,}115.93$  
Interest $\approx \$10{,}115.93$  
Fee $=2\%\times 80{,}000=\$1{,}600$  
Total cost $\approx \$11{,}715.93$

Loan C has the lowest total cost, despite the higher APR, because of the much shorter term and lower fee than Loan B.
